evidence_note: Heavy overnight rainfall left settlements houses markets and Radio Benue facilities submerged in Makurdi.
NEMA described the Kogi flood situation as devastating and advised floodplain residents to relocate.
Houses in Yenagoa were reported submerged after two days of torrential rain.
Vice President flood assessment reported visibly rising flood conditions including Onitsha.
Sentinel-2 imagery showed flooded crop areas along the Hadejia River on 22 September 2018.
Bayelsa governor assessed flooded communities in Yenagoa and Southern Ijaw before ordering school closures.
Sentinel-1 flood extent was acquired over Doma Makurdi and Guma on 25 to 26 September 2022.
Homes roads and farmland in Lokoja communities including Adankolo Ganaja Kabawa and Gadumo were already submerged by 28 September 2022.
NEMA and Bayelsa SEMA assessment documented Akenfa in Yenagoa LGA among communities affected by flooding on 30 September 2022.
A nearly 12-hour downpour flooded Wurukum Achusa Gboko Road and access to Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University in Makurdi.
Flooding overran hostels and paralysed activities at the Metallurgical Training Institute in Onitsha.
Obogoro community in Yenagoa LGA was among communities reported to be suffering hardship caused by flood.
Multiple Yenagoa neighbourhoods including Cemetery Azikoro Ekeki Okaka Swali Kpansia Amarata and Ovom were submerged by flash floods.
NSCDC reported a flooded river in Hadejia on 7 September 2024 with a fatal drowning and warned against flooded rivers and ponds.
NEMA visited Lokoja during the active Kogi flood response; emergency shelters around Lokoja were accommodating displaced persons and rescue evacuation operations were active.
